etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From French didactique, from Ancient Greek διδακτικός (didaktikós, “skilled in teaching”), from διδακτός (didaktós, “taught, learnt”), from διδάσκω (didáskō, “to teach, educate”). By surface analysis, didact +‎ -ic.
senses: Instructive or intended to teach or demonstrate, especially with regard to morality.
(archaic) A treatise on teaching or education.
